text: What I would want is immediate suspension, in the same way that criminals are denied bail pending sentence, but I concede that doesn't work well in an ongoing sporting season....  But it has been agreed (well, City whined about it obv, but lost) that the sanctions hearing will proceed in parallel with the appeal - although I don't think the rules are clear on timelines in that circumstance.  To your point though, the sanctions are decided by the original commission, having heard from the PL (about obstruction, delay and aggravating factors) and from City (we're innocent anyway, so just give us a fine) at a sanctions hearing.  How a partial appeal victory would affect what would potentially be a macro punishment (eg expulsion) would be hard to deal with, as you imply - but to be realistic, City will try and appeal the sanction as well, and will be trying to go to court on the guilty verdict as well.  So your original point - that the sanctions are known but are under wraps pending an appeal result, MAY become true in the future, but I think it's a bit soon for that....for the reasons I gave. It could also be that when the sanctions are decided, they DO become public, which would then (IMO) serve to significantly accelerate City's appetite for getting to a resolution - in short, they'll delay until a punishment is applied, and then they'll be in a huge rush to get that punishment stripped.

They then win promotion - for what? A year chipping 40-60 points off their "debt"? Good luck motivating the players for that.  Every match they played in the PL would be a pointless exercise for both sides, all the supporters, and the TV - yes, City might win, but nobody will be interested.  Then, it'd take at least 5 PL seasons to "pay off" the points. Factor in the Championship years in between those and you've got nine years of a player's career yo-yoing between meaningless seasons and vaguely interesting ones. That's horrible - and it won't be the players who won the things that go through that. It won't even be the current squad - it'll be whatever bunch of journeymen they can afford (even if not fined, removal of their fake sponsorship slashes their funding capabilities).  That's cruel and unusual punishment, and I genuinely think City would have a case that was unfair. And for context I think they could have no complaints if their titles were stripped and they were pushed down into non-league.
